title: Skip entries whose round-trip stop-exit cost exceeds 0.15R (Primary's 8 setups)
hypothesis: Trades with a small stop distance per share pay 1c+1bp per side plus 2c stop slippage on a tiny R, so costs (not signal quality) sink them; removing cost > 0.15R raises net R without touching signals.
notes: Two-year open history, costs in, portfolio sim of Primary's 8 setups: parent -0.070R (t -4.60, n 29,285); A3 -0.026R, paired daily delta +3.49R/day t 8.17, train +3.76 / valid +3.15, up +6.51 / down +0.55. Locked block, look 1 (the only look): parent -0.112R, A3 -0.053R, delta +4.46R/day t 4.31 -> PASS of the improvement bar. BUT the filtered book is still negative after costs on two years and on the locked block; removed trades have the same gross edge (+0.012 vs +0.016R) - the gain is cost avoidance. Live 10 sessions (paper, descriptive): current-8 trades with cost > 0.15R made +43.7R / +$471 (10-22 dominated), so live would have lost by it. N 19, bar 2.43. Owner decision; not live.

title: Cross-setup correlation caps (1 lot/symbol, 1 entry/symbol/day, 2 same-side lots/sector ETF, 3 entries/poll)
hypothesis: Type B (same symbol / sector losers across setups in a 30-min window) was 52% of Primary's loser $ over 10-15..10-28; caps should cut the stacked loss.
notes: 4 configs on two years (Primary 8 setups): deltas +1.29..+2.02R/day, t 3.09..3.65, positive in train and valid and up sessions but NEGATIVE in down sessions (-0.12..-1.46R/day) and shrunk avg R worse than the parent in train for 2 of 4 (B1, B2) -> fail the pre-declared gate. Live Type B was mostly setups no longer in Primary (NS2 10-15, NS3-FD 10-21). Related: nightly-1028-ns3-family-one-bet.

title: Primary 8 setups: flatten 15:45 / 15:30, 15:00 stop tighten 0.5R, 15:45 longs only
